es: Detectar pistas de que un narrador no es fiable y deducir qué pasó realmente con must have, can't have y might have.

teaching.en: An unreliable narrator says he was at home, but his muddy boots are a clue.
teaching.es: Un narrador poco fiable dice que estaba en casa, pero sus botas embarradas son una pista.
teaching.explanationEs: Una pista (clue) es un detalle que apunta a la verdad y choca con lo que cuenta el narrador.
segments: An unreliable narrator says he was at home,
but his muddy boots are a clue.
teaching.audioText: An unreliable narrator says he was at home, but his muddy boots are a clue.

teaching.en: His version of the night contradicts the letter on the table.
teaching.es: Su versión de la noche contradice la carta que hay sobre la mesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Contradict: lo que muestra un detalle choca con lo que dice el narrador.
segments: His version of the night contradicts
the letter on the table.
teaching.audioText: His version of the night contradicts the letter on the table.

teaching.en: The narrator claims he never left, but the ticket in his coat must have come from somewhere.
teaching.es: El narrador afirma que nunca salió, pero el billete de su abrigo tiene que haber venido de algún sitio.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado.
segments: The narrator claims he never left, but the ticket
in his coat must have come from somewhere.
teaching.audioText: The narrator claims he never left, but the ticket in his coat must have come from somewhere.

teaching.en: He can't have forgotten the meeting; his calm voice is suspicious.
teaching.es: No puede haberse olvidado de la reunión; su voz tranquila resulta sospechosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: casi seguro que no ocurrió. Para deducir no se usa mustn't.
segments: He can't have forgotten the meeting;
his calm voice is suspicious.
teaching.audioText: He can't have forgotten the meeting; his calm voice is suspicious.

teaching.en: The narrator might have exaggerated the storm to seem brave.
teaching.es: Puede que el narrador exagerara la tormenta para parecer valiente.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posibilidad sin certeza. Exaggerate es contar algo como más grande de lo que fue.
segments: The narrator might have exaggerated
the storm to seem brave.
teaching.audioText: The narrator might have exaggerated the storm to seem brave.

teaching.en: He could have tried to conceal the letter, or he might simply have lost it.
teaching.es: Podría haber intentado ocultar la carta, o quizá simplemente la perdió.
teaching.explanationEs: Could have y might have plantean explicaciones posibles; conceal significa ocultar.
segments: He could have tried to conceal the letter,
or he might simply have lost it.
teaching.audioText: He could have tried to conceal the letter, or he might simply have lost it.

prompt.es: El narrador dice que no salió, pero tiene barro en las botas. ¿Qué deduces?

choices.text: He mustn't have gone out.
He must go out.
He must have gone out.

feedback.es: Must have + participio deduce algo pasado casi seguro, y el barro de las botas lo apoya.

hint.es: Es una deducción sobre el pasado: modal + have + participio.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su versión de la noche contradice la carta.»

feedback.es: La versión es la manera en que alguien cuenta lo ocurrido, y aquí la carta la contradice.

hint.es: Es la palabra para la forma particular de contar los hechos.

origin.text: His ___ of the night contradicts the letter.

prompt.es: Ordena: «No puede haber estado en casa toda la noche.»

answer.text: He can't have been at home all night

feedback.es: El negativo de la deducción sobre el pasado se forma con can't have + participio.

hint.es: Después del sujeto va can't, luego have y el participio been.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su grado de certeza.

pairs.es: Casi seguro que no lo sabía.
Quizá lo sabía, pero no es seguro.

feedback.es: Must y can't expresan casi certeza; might deja la posibilidad abierta.

pairs.es: Casi seguro que no lo sabía.
Quizá lo sabía, pero no es seguro.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye la hablante.

choices.text: Mark's gym story is probably false.
Mark probably lost his phone at the gym.
Mark will come back from the gym soon.

feedback.es: La hablante suma dos pistas, el móvil en la cocina y los zapatos secos, y concluye con can't have.

origin.audio: Mark says he spent the evening at the gym. But his phone stayed in the kitchen, and his shoes are dry. He can't have been there.

prompt.es: Completa: «Puede que el narrador exagerara la tormenta.»

feedback.es: Might have + participio de exaggerate plantea que el narrador contó la tormenta como peor de lo que fue.

origin.text: The narrator might have ___ the storm.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pista contradice la versión del narrador?

choices.text: He read until midnight.
His coat was wet with rain.
He went to bed.

feedback.es: Un abrigo mojado por la lluvia sugiere que salió, y eso contradice su versión de que nunca salió.

origin.text: «I never left the flat,» said Tom. «I read until midnight and went to bed.» Next morning, the police found his coat behind the door, wet with rain.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sospecha la hablante de Leo.

choices.text: He wrote the diary himself.
He met her only once.
He is hiding that he knew her.

feedback.es: El nombre de Leo aparece seis veces en el diario, por eso la hablante cree que oculta que la conocía.

origin.audio: Leo told us he had never met the owner. But his name is written in her diary six times. He can't be telling the whole truth.

prompt.es: Completa: «No puede haber sido un accidente.»

feedback.es: La deducción negativa sobre el pasado se forma con can't have + participio.

origin.text: It ___ have been an accident.

prompt.es: Escribe dos deducciones sobre el narrador; apoya la primera en una pista.

answer.text: He must have gone out, because his boots are muddy. He might have exaggerated the story to seem brave.
accepted: He must have gone out, because his boots are muddy. He might have exaggerated the story to seem brave.
He must have left the flat, because there is a train ticket in his coat. He could have lied about the evening.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta apoya cada deducción en una pista: must have con las botas o el billete, might o could have para una posibilidad.

origin.text: Un narrador dice que pasó la noche en casa, pero sus botas están embarradas y tiene un billete de tren en el abrigo. Escribe dos frases: una con must have, apoyada en una pista, y otra con might have.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El narrador podría haber ocultado la carta.»

answer.text: The narrator could have concealed the letter

feedback.es: Could have + participio expresa una posibilidad sobre algo que el narrador pudo hacer.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del narrador suena menos fiable?

choices.text: I promise I never went near the river, not even once, not even for a second!
I left the house at eight and came back at ten.
I am not sure what time I came home.

feedback.es: Insistir de forma exagerada, sin que nadie lo pida, es una señal típica de un narrador poco fiable.

prompt.es: Completa: «Afirma que nunca estuvo allí, pero su abrigo sigue en la habitación.»

feedback.es: Claim presenta lo que dice el narrador como algo dudoso, justo antes de la pista que lo contradice.

origin.text: He ___ he was never there, but his coat is still in the room.

es: Usar con precisión el vocabulario de análisis literario (motif, symbol, theme, foreshadowing, imagery, resonate) en una reseña crítica.

teaching.en: The recurring motif of water in the novel suggests change.
teaching.es: El motivo recurrente del agua en la novela sugiere cambio.
teaching.explanationEs: Un motif es una imagen o idea que se repite a lo largo de la obra.
segments: The recurring motif of water
in the novel suggests change.
teaching.audioText: The recurring motif of water in the novel suggests change.

teaching.en: The broken clock is a symbol of time that has been lost.
teaching.es: El reloj roto es un símbolo del tiempo que se ha perdido.
teaching.explanationEs: Un symbol es una cosa concreta que representa una idea.
segments: The broken clock is a symbol
of time that has been lost.
teaching.audioText: The broken clock is a symbol of time that has been lost.

teaching.en: The storm in chapter two is foreshadowing: it warns us that something bad will happen.
teaching.es: La tormenta del capítulo dos es un presagio: nos avisa de que ocurrirá algo malo.
teaching.explanationEs: Foreshadowing anticipa lo que vendrá sin decirlo abiertamente.
segments: The storm in chapter two is foreshadowing: it
warns us that something bad will happen.
teaching.audioText: The storm in chapter two is foreshadowing: it warns us that something bad will happen.

teaching.en: The main theme is the cost of ambition.
teaching.es: El tema principal es el precio de la ambición.
teaching.explanationEs: El theme es la idea general que sostiene toda la obra.
segments: The main theme is
the cost of ambition.
teaching.audioText: The main theme is the cost of ambition.

teaching.en: The writer's cold, grey imagery makes the town feel lonely.
teaching.es: Las imágenes frías y grises del autor hacen que el pueblo parezca solitario.
teaching.explanationEs: Imagery son las imágenes sensoriales que crean una atmósfera.
segments: The writer's cold, grey imagery
makes the town feel lonely.
teaching.audioText: The writer's cold, grey imagery makes the town feel lonely.

teaching.en: The final chapter will resonate with anyone who has left home.
teaching.es: El último capítulo calará en cualquiera que haya dejado su casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Resonate with + persona: la obra le llega y le dice algo.
segments: The final chapter will resonate with
anyone who has left home.
teaching.audioText: The final chapter will resonate with anyone who has left home.

prompt.es: Completa: «El tema principal es el precio de la ambición.»

feedback.es: El tema es la idea general que sostiene la obra, como el precio de la ambición.

hint.es: Es la idea central de toda la obra, no un objeto concreto.

origin.text: The main ___ is the cost of ambition.

prompt.es: ¿Qué término describe una imagen que reaparece a lo largo de la novela?

choices.text: motif
foreshadowing
theme

feedback.es: El motif es el elemento que se repite; el tema es la idea y el presagio anticipa algo.

hint.es: Piensa en algo que aparece una y otra vez.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El reloj roto es un símbolo del tiempo perdido.»

answer.text: The broken clock is a symbol of lost time

feedback.es: El patrón para dar significado a una cosa concreta es «is a symbol of» + idea.

hint.es: Después del sujeto va is a symbol of, y al final la idea.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada término con su definición.

pairs.es: una cosa que representa una idea
una pista de lo que pasará después

feedback.es: Cada término cubre un nivel distinto del análisis: repetición, representación, anticipación y atmósfera.

pairs.es: una cosa que representa una idea
una pista de lo que pasará después

prompt.es: Completa: «La tormenta del capítulo dos es un presagio.»

feedback.es: Una tormenta que avisa de una desgracia posterior es un ejemplo de foreshadowing.

origin.text: The storm in chapter two is ___.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la hablante con las puertas.

choices.text: She explains that the ending is about a door.
She points out a detail that repeats through the book.
She complains that the story has too many doors.

feedback.es: La hablante observa que las puertas reaparecen y lo llama motif, es decir, un elemento recurrente.

origin.audio: The writer keeps returning to doors: open doors, closed doors, a door painted red. It is a motif that builds a feeling of choice and fear.

prompt.es: Completa cuatro frases de una reseña crítica con el término literario adecuado.

feedback.es: Central pide theme, una cosa que representa una idea pide symbol, lo que se repite pide motif y las imágenes que crean atmósfera piden imagery.

sentences: The white dress is a ___ of a fresh start.
The recurring ___ of mirrors shows how people see themselves.
The writer's dark, wet ___ makes the ending feel sad.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recurso describe la hablante.

choices.text: The bird is the narrator of the story.
The bird is the main theme of the book.
The bird warns of something that happens later.

feedback.es: El pájaro anuncia la desaparición posterior sin decirlo: es foreshadowing.

origin.audio: The opening scene shows a black bird on the roof. Later, a neighbour disappears. The bird was a warning of what would come.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que usa bien resonate.

choices.text: The final chapter resonates with anyone who has lost a friend.
The final chapter resonates to anyone who has lost a friend.
The final chapter resonates anyone who has lost a friend.

feedback.es: Resonate se construye con with seguido de la persona a la que le llega la obra.

prompt.es: Escribe dos frases de reseña: un símbolo y un efecto en el lector.

answer.text: The dark lighthouse is a symbol of lost hope. The ending will resonate with anyone who has felt alone.
accepted: The dark lighthouse is a symbol of lost hope. The ending will resonate with anyone who has felt alone.
The lighthouse is a symbol of hope that has been lost. The story resonates with many readers.

feedback.es: Una buena reseña nombra el símbolo con is a symbol of y valora su efecto con resonate with.

origin.text: Reseña de una novela: el faro apagado simboliza la esperanza perdida. Escribe dos frases: una con is a symbol of y otra con resonate with.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La imaginería fría transmite una sensación de miedo.»

answer.text: The cold imagery conveys a sense of fear

feedback.es: Convey + sensación expresa qué efecto produce la imagery en el lector.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe algo sutil.

choices.text: The writer tells us the whole ending in the first line.
The writer hints at the ending in a subtle way, with one small detail.
The writer shouts the ending on every page.

feedback.es: Lo sutil se insinúa con un detalle pequeño, sin decirlo abiertamente.

prompt.es: Completa: «El agua es un símbolo recurrente en el libro.»

feedback.es: Recurring describe lo que vuelve a aparecer una y otra vez, como el agua en el libro.

title.en: Characters, plot and point of view
title.es: Personajes, trama y punto de vista

es: Identificar narrador, motivación, tema, tono e inferencia en un fragmento de relato, respondiendo con pruebas del texto.

teaching.en: The protagonist tells the story in the first person, so we only see her viewpoint.
teaching.es: La protagonista cuenta la historia en primera persona, así que solo vemos su punto de vista.
teaching.explanationEs: Primera persona es «I»; el viewpoint es desde dónde se ve toda la historia.
segments: The protagonist tells the story in the first
person, so we only see her viewpoint.
teaching.audioText: The protagonist tells the story in the first person, so we only see her viewpoint.

teaching.en: Her motivation is simple: she wants to prove that her brother was wrong.
teaching.es: Su motivación es sencilla: quiere demostrar que su hermano se equivocaba.
teaching.explanationEs: Motivation es lo que el personaje quiere y le hace actuar.
segments: Her motivation is simple: she wants to
prove that her brother was wrong.
teaching.audioText: Her motivation is simple: she wants to prove that her brother was wrong.

teaching.en: The tone of the passage is bitter, because every memory ends in a complaint.
teaching.es: El tono del fragmento es amargo, porque cada recuerdo acaba en una queja.
teaching.explanationEs: El tone es la actitud que transmite el texto: amargo, tenso, cariñoso...
segments: The tone of the passage is bitter,
because every memory ends in a complaint.
teaching.audioText: The tone of the passage is bitter, because every memory ends in a complaint.

teaching.en: We can infer that she is reluctant to go back, because she keeps checking the time.
teaching.es: Podemos inferir que no quiere volver, porque no deja de mirar la hora.
teaching.explanationEs: Infer: deducir algo que el texto no dice, a partir de una pista del propio texto.
segments: We can infer that she is reluctant to
go back, because she keeps checking the time.
teaching.audioText: We can infer that she is reluctant to go back, because she keeps checking the time.

teaching.en: The plot follows one week in which an old betrayal comes back.
teaching.es: La trama sigue una semana en la que regresa una vieja traición.
teaching.explanationEs: Plot es lo que ocurre y en qué orden; betrayal es traición.
segments: The plot follows one week in
which an old betrayal comes back.
teaching.audioText: The plot follows one week in which an old betrayal comes back.

prompt.es: ¿Quién cuenta esta historia?

choices.text: Nora, in the first person.
An outside narrator who reports what Nora does.
Nora's father, in the first person.

feedback.es: El texto dice «Nora drove» y «she smiled»: la cuenta alguien de fuera, en tercera persona.

hint.es: Fíjate en los pronombres: el texto dice I o dice she y he.

origin.text: Every Sunday, Nora drove her father to the lake, and every Sunday he told the same story about the fish he never caught. She smiled, nodded and looked at her phone. One day, he stopped talking. The silence was the loudest thing she had ever heard.

prompt.es: ¿Qué se puede inferir del final del fragmento?

choices.text: She is relieved that the stories are over.
She is angry because he never caught a fish.
She now misses her father's repeated stories.

feedback.es: Que el silencio sea «the loudest thing» indica que ahora echa de menos las historias repetidas.

hint.es: Mira la última frase: ¿el silencio le resulta agradable o doloroso?

origin.text: Every Sunday, Nora drove her father to the lake, and every Sunday he told the same story about the fish he never caught. She smiled, nodded and looked at her phone. One day, he stopped talking. The silence was the loudest thing she had ever heard.

feedback.es: La motivación es la razón que impulsa al personaje a actuar.

hint.es: Es la razón que empuja al personaje a hacer algo.

origin.text: Nora's ___ is to spend time with her father.

choices.text: Tense and uncertain
Playful and relaxed
Angry and cold

feedback.es: Leo repite «I'm fine» y duda ante la oferta, lo que crea un tono tenso e incierto.

origin.text: «I'm fine,» said Leo for the third time, and he closed the laptop. On the screen, the job offer was still open. His mother was calling from the kitchen, but he pretended not to hear. If he said yes, he would leave the city; if he said no, he would stay in the only place where he felt safe.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La trama sigue a un joven que no puede decidirse.»

answer.text: The plot follows a young man who cannot decide

feedback.es: Plot designa lo que ocurre en la historia; aquí, un joven atrapado entre dos decisiones.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo duda en aceptar el trabajo, porque se siente seguro en su ciudad.»

feedback.es: Reluctant describe a quien duda o no quiere hacer algo, como Leo con la oferta.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se puede inferir de la abuela.

choices.text: She forgot about the letters.
She treasured the letters, especially the last one.
She read the letters to the family every year.

feedback.es: Guardó todas las cartas en una caja azul y solo la última estaba abierta: de ahí se infiere que las apreciaba.

origin.audio: My grandmother kept every letter my grandfather wrote from the sea. She never read them aloud, and she never threw them away. After she died, we found them in a blue box, and only the last one was open.

prompt.es: ¿Qué punto de vista tiene el fragmento?

choices.text: Third person: an outsider describes Ana.
Second person: someone speaks to Ana.
First person: the narrator tells his own secret.

feedback.es: El narrador usa «I never told Ana»: habla de sí mismo y de su secreto en primera persona.

origin.text: I never told Ana that I had read her diary. For years I smiled at her at dinner, knowing what she thought of me. Was it regret that made me quiet, or was it fear that she would find out?

feedback.es: Una inferencia correcta empieza con We can infer that y se apoya en una pista del texto con because.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el tema del fragmento?

choices.text: Community and support in hard times.
The danger of fire.
Being alone is always best.

feedback.es: Los vecinos ayudan sin que nadie lo pida: el tema es la comunidad y el apoyo mutuo.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La protagonista quiere demostrar que su hermano se equivocaba.»

answer.text: The protagonist wants to prove her brother wrong

es: Reseñar una película con descripción, dos deducciones sobre personajes, valoración con pruebas, un defecto y una recomendación.

teaching.en: The plot is gripping from the first scene, and the pacing never drops.
teaching.es: La trama engancha desde la primera escena y el ritmo nunca decae.
teaching.explanationEs: Gripping es lo que atrapa al espectador; el pacing es el ritmo al que avanza la historia.
segments: The plot is gripping from the first
scene, and the pacing never drops.
teaching.audioText: The plot is gripping from the first scene, and the pacing never drops.

teaching.en: The lead actor gives a convincing performance; he must have lived through something similar.
teaching.es: El actor principal da una interpretación convincente; debió de vivir algo parecido.
teaching.explanationEs: Give a performance: dar una interpretación. La deducción con must have apoya la valoración.
segments: The lead actor gives a convincing performance;
he must have lived through something similar.
teaching.audioText: The lead actor gives a convincing performance; he must have lived through something similar.

teaching.en: Her calm performance suggests that she can't have been surprised by the news.
teaching.es: Su interpretación serena sugiere que no pudo sorprenderse con la noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio deduce, a partir de lo que vemos, algo que casi seguro no ocurrió.
segments: Her calm performance suggests that she can't
have been surprised by the news.
teaching.audioText: Her calm performance suggests that she can't have been surprised by the news.

teaching.en: The ending feels rushed, but it is a minor flaw in a stunning film.
teaching.es: El final parece apresurado, pero es un defecto menor en una película impresionante.
teaching.explanationEs: Rushed es demasiado rápido; reconocer un flaw da credibilidad a la reseña.
segments: The ending feels rushed, but it is
a minor flaw in a stunning film.
teaching.audioText: The ending feels rushed, but it is a minor flaw in a stunning film.

teaching.en: Although the dialogue is sometimes predictable, the cast is excellent.
teaching.es: Aunque el diálogo a veces es previsible, el reparto es excelente.
teaching.explanationEs: Although introduce una concesión; predictable es lo que se adivina de antemano.
segments: Although the dialogue is sometimes
predictable, the cast is excellent.
teaching.audioText: Although the dialogue is sometimes predictable, the cast is excellent.

teaching.en: I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys slow, thoughtful stories.
teaching.es: Se la recomendaría a cualquiera que disfrute de las historias lentas y reflexivas.
teaching.explanationEs: Recommend it to + persona: la recomendación nombra a quién va dirigida.
segments: I would recommend it to anyone
who enjoys slow, thoughtful stories.
teaching.audioText: I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys slow, thoughtful stories.

choices.text: The plot is gripping.
I liked it because I liked it.
The plot is gripping: in the first scene, the main character loses everything.

hint.es: Busca la frase que da un ejemplo de la película.

prompt.es: Completa: «El ritmo es lento, pero la trama es absorbente.»

feedback.es: El pacing es la velocidad a la que avanza la historia.

hint.es: Es la velocidad a la que avanza la historia.

answer.text: The lead actor gives a convincing performance

hint.es: El verbo es gives y performance va al final.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada término de reseña con su significado.

feedback.es: Estos cuatro términos valoran la trama, la sorpresa, la calidad y los puntos débiles.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante de la película.

choices.text: She enjoys it, with one small complaint about the middle.
She thinks the ending is predictable.
She gives it the highest mark.

feedback.es: Elogia el reparto y el final, y solo critica el ritmo de la parte central, por eso le da cuatro de cinco.

origin.audio: The cast is excellent, and the ending is stunning. However, the pacing is a little slow in the middle, so I give it four out of five.

feedback.es: Como no conoce el final, la deducción negativa sobre el pasado se forma con can't have + participio.

origin.text: He ___ have seen the film; he does not know the ending.

prompt.es: Escribe una reseña: deducciones, valoración con ejemplo, defecto y recomendación.

answer.text: The Last Train is a quiet film about a woman who waits alone at an empty station every night. The plot is gripping, and the lead actor gives a convincing performance. For example, she never gets on the train, so she must have been waiting for someone special. Her calm voice also suggests that she can't have been surprised by the ending, and she might have known the truth from the start. Although the pacing is slow and the ending feels rushed, these are minor flaws in a stunning film. The cast is excellent, and the story is never predictable, so I was never bored. The music is simple, but the silence says more than any dialogue, and I was moved by the last scene. In short, it is a thoughtful film with a strong central idea. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys slow, thoughtful stories, and I would give it four out of five.

I watched The Last Train last night, and it is a stunning story about a woman who waits at an empty station. The lead actor gives a convincing performance, and the plot is gripping from the first scene. For instance, she never gets on the train, so she must have lost someone she loved. She can't have been surprised by the news at the end, because she never asks a question, and she might have hoped for a different ending. Although the pacing is slow, the cast is excellent, and the story is never predictable. The ending feels rushed, but that is a small flaw in a thoughtful film. I recommend it to anyone who likes quiet stories about people, and I would happily watch it again.

answer.text: I would argue that the ending of The Blue Door is ambiguous on purpose. The narrator says that nobody ever lived in the house, but he can't have been honest, because he also says that his sister left after an argument. The wet letter is a clue: she must have written it in a hurry, and he might have hidden it for years. In my reading, the blue door is a symbol of a memory that he cannot close. Carlos thinks the narrator is lying to us, and I concede that this is plausible. However, I am not convinced that the book wants us to be certain. The writer hides an important detail in a subtle way, and the imagery of cold and rain makes the sadness resonate with readers. It is a thoughtful novel, although the pacing is slow in the middle, and I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys a gripping story with a difficult ending. Fair enough, Carlos: we will have to agree to disagree.

I would argue that the last scene is ambiguous, and I read it as a symbol of memory. The narrator can't have been telling the whole truth, because the letter was wet, so someone must have read it or hidden it. His sister might have left in anger, and he might have closed the blue door to forget her. Carlos says that the narrator is lying, and I concede that this is plausible, because the clues contradict him. Even so, I am not convinced that the writer wants a clear answer.
